mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses equity discount rates by reducing risk-free rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate above 7.5% within one month signals labor market deterioration, triggering corporate earnings contraction and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises above 7.5% in one month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in consumer credit (RSAFS) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates demand shock from reduced spending power, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days through profit margin compression.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or interaction Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rate hikes compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 98.0 within one month signals manufacturing contraction, leading to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls below 98.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In housing market recovery (HOUST > 900.0), increased residential construction drives consumer spending growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST exceeds 900.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days through reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or interaction Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained housing starts above 900.0 signal strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST exceeds 900.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.
